assumptions: Positive createPrerequisite protocol projected onto one organization/logical-operation key, two transaction callers, two scope/merchant pairs, one owned allowance-period identity, opaque digests/keys 0..1 and integer currency inputs 0..2. References 0/1 belong to the projected owner; reference 2 is foreign. The model uses one field for requested_amount/reserved_amount, whose equality is enforced by the writer and schema.

Every distinct valid bounded record is enumerated. Invalid arguments collapse to unchanged transaction abort, and terminal replay payloads collapse to unchanged replay or rejection; general actions retain all guards and negative scenarios.

The caller has locked the organization and supplies the reservation/allocations from the same transaction. Repository calls stage complete results; any failure aborts the whole owning transaction, and commit publishes all staged writes atomically.
Canonical fixed-six money is abstracted as integer units; parsing, precision, numeric overflow, cryptographic digest binding and SQL isolation are not proved.
Expiry labels represent valid caller-supplied deadlines. Actual time, expiry validation and clock progression are not represented.

The repository neither owns purchased balances nor validates economic meaning of referenced ledger rows. Caller-owned debit/refund and allowance eligibility/expiry decisions are assumptions; no repository-level overspend or provider-effect proof is claimed.

The caller-supplied allowanceExpired flag controls unused allowance classification. Expired allowance is not a purchased-credit refund; purchased releases remain purchased credit. Actual clocks, grace windows and cross-operation reference uniqueness are outside this model.

Reference IDs are owned alpha representatives per field role. persistCurrent reuses reserveRef symbolically; it does not assert that real reservation, settlement and refund ledger rows share identity. Independent reference-identity and uniqueness coverage remain excluded.

The strict conformance hook runs four ordered transaction cases and two independently seeded cancellation/expiry cases on PGlite and fresh dedicated_compute_test_* PostgreSQL databases. It verifies committed allocation conservation and excludes unrelated skipped/filtered cases from selected coverage.
bounds.progress: No fairness or temporal progress claim. Safety covers only the declared finite row protocol.
